clue.text: Writer I included in child's number

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting inside it, so the writer and I go within the child

parts.note: a child may be a son
a quill is a pen, something that writes

explanation.surface: Someone inserts themselves, a writer, into a child's phone number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is not a phone number but the definition: a jokily huge, unspecified quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: A made-up word for an enormous but vague count, used informally as a large quantity.

clue.text: Copper in search around East End finding no Ripper victim?

indicators.note: the copper symbol is placed inside the word for search
in London's East End the Cockney accent drops initial aitches, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a hunt is a search
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman searching the East End finds no victim of Jack the Ripper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman in a Ripper hunt, but it is the element. The Ripper slashed his victims; one not slashed is literally not cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack the Ripper cut his victims, so someone who escaped him would be whole and unslashed.

clue.text: Sort of grain initially burst when one walked on one

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a mat is something people walk on
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Grain bursts open when someone treads on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-grain rice variety from South Asia, a type of cereal grain.

clue.text: Foul that almost crippled rugby player

indicators.note: crippled suggests something bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word falls one letter short of complete

explanation.surface: A foul tackle very nearly crippled a rugby player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THAT to THA, which joins FOUL to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union an out-half is the fly-half, a player position behind the scrum.

clue.text: Tear seen after touching new performance

indicators.note: one word is placed after the other in the answer

parts.note: re means concerning or touching on
to tear is to run quickly

explanation.surface: A tear appears after someone is moved by a fresh show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' suggests crying, but here it is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeat showing of a programme, a performance given afresh.

clue.text: Dare, perhaps, to interrupt a speech provider, skipping

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something

parts.note: the voice is what provides speech
Dan Dare is a British comic-strip space hero, so Dare suggests Dan

explanation.surface: A dare is used to interrupt someone giving a speech, who skips it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan Dare was the star of the British boys' comic Eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging or skipping something is the act of steering clear of it, a noun sense.

clue.text: Kid on horse that's fed on good spicy food

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
a horse fed on something has it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat
to kid is to josh, to tease

explanation.surface: A child rides a horse that has been fed well, alongside spicy food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is the verb to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kashmiri curry of lamb in a rich, aromatic sauce, a spiced dish.

clue.text: Girl programmed to return hugs

indicators.note: returning means the extracted letters are read backwards
the word programmed hugs the letters within it

explanation.surface: A girl has been programmed to go back to hugging.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as in Jane Austen's heroine, so a girl.

clue.text: Cheers on lawman providing evidence?

indicators.note: in an across clue the second piece put on the first follows it

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney
ta is British slang for thanks or cheers

explanation.surface: A toast to a lawman who is supplying evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts and figures collected for analysis serve as evidence, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Giving due respect to kind Republican front runner

parts.note: pace, from Latin, means with due respect to someone
make means kind or brand

explanation.surface: A deferential nod to a kindly Republican who leads the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pace' (two syllables) is used when politely disagreeing with someone named.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race the runner who sets the speed at the front is a pace-setter.

clue.text: Quickly turned on radio after failure to catch talent contest

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a miss is a failure to catch

indicators.note: words on the radio are heard rather than seen, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: whirled means spun round quickly

explanation.surface: A broadcaster switches on the radio after missing a talent show.
explanation.definitionFit: A global beauty pageant, a competition judged partly on talent.

clue.text: Generous NCO informally changing shilling for pound

indicators.note: changing one thing for another swaps a letter in the word

parts.note: sarge is the casual name for a sergeant, a non-commissioned officer
S stood for shilling in old British money
L, from libra, stands for pound

explanation.surface: A big-hearted sergeant swaps his shilling for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin. 'for' sits between the old and new letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Large can mean liberal or big-hearted, as in a large spirit, hence generous.

clue.text: Puccini's soldier — anarchist primarily, pacifist second

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word

parts.note: a CO is a conscientious objector, a pacifist
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A soldier in a Puccini opera is first an anarchist, then a pacifist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puccini's' is the definition: the composer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Puccini was christened with this Italian given name, so it is his.

clue.text: Out of water bottles pennies gradually dropped

indicators.note: bottling something keeps it inside, so the pennies go within

parts.note: something dried is out of water
P is penny, so PP is pennies

explanation.surface: Without water, coins are slowly let fall into bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling slowly in drops describes liquid coming out bit by bit.

clue.text: Patron saint lives on earth

indicators.note: in an across clue the piece put on the other follows it

parts.note: a fox's earth is its den
is can mean lives or exists

explanation.surface: A patron saint living here on earth.
explanation.walkthrough: St Denis is the patron saint of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Denis, the martyred bishop of Paris, is the patron saint of France.

clue.text: Cosmetic used on spots that hurt

indicators.note: the following piece is placed after the earlier ones in this across answer

parts.note: to spot is to see, so spots means eyes as a verb
had means used, as in had a car
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A cosmetic applied to blemishes that sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like pimples, but it is the verb meaning sees.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured powder applied to the eyelids, a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Greet dual monarchy, evidently more moderate

parts.note: greet is Scots for weep, to sob

indicators.note: dual means the piece appears twice

parts.note: ER stands for the reigning monarch, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Welcoming a joint monarchy is plainly a more temperate choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greet' looks like a welcome, but it is the Scots word for cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Less drunk or less extreme, a comparative meaning calmer and more temperate.

clue.text: Bus pass not needed, oddly, for peak times?

indicators.note: the odd letters are dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A bus pass isn't needed at peak hours.
explanation.definitionFit: High points in fortune are highs, the good spells contrasted with downs.

clue.text: Picking up and taking home 24 caps

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece capping another sits on top of it

parts.note: the 24-across answer means generous; its clothing-size abbreviation is L
taking home pay is earning

explanation.surface: Collecting the take-home pay along with 24 caps.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' refers to the answer of 24-across, abbreviated as a clothing size.
explanation.definitionFit: Picking up a skill is acquiring knowledge, the same as gaining it through study.

clue.text: Current affairs commonly avoided at first in holiday location

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
biz is a slangy word for business, affairs

indicators.note: at first picks out the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Topical matters are steered clear of at first in a resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balearic island famed as a Mediterranean holiday resort.

clue.text: Tiepolo's exterior echoing ornate architectural style

indicators.note: ornate suggests elaborate reworking, so the letters are rearranged
the exterior of the word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: The outside of a Tiepolo painting echoes an elaborate building style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior' gives TO, which joins ECHOING to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival of medieval pointed-arch building, a style of architecture.

clue.text: Guys endlessly keeping books and papers in a mess

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside
endlessly means the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Blokes keep books and papers in a disorganised heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims GUYS to UY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mess means disordered and cluttered, the opposite of neat.

clue.text: Compulsive drag performer is man cavorting in necklace

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed inside the necklace word

parts.note: a choker is a close-fitting necklace

indicators.note: cavorting suggests prancing about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drag act features a man prancing around in a necklace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' means a pull on a cigarette, not cross-dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lights one cigarette after another, compulsively taking drags.

clue.text: On top of cheese, turned up rich material

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue turned up means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: rich food is fat
feta is a Greek cheese

explanation.surface: Rich fabric is laid on top of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisp, lustrous silk fabric, a type of material.

clue.text: This well resembling a waterfall?

parts.note: a phrase meaning perfectly healthy, read literally as falling vertically like rain does

explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom for perfectly well, in good health again.

clue.text: Accepting new pressure, our attitude is determined

indicators.note: accepting means taking something inside

parts.note: taken as written
N is new
P is pressure
a pose is an attitude or stance

explanation.surface: Taking on fresh pressure, our stance becomes resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: N and P go inside OUR, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Done deliberately, decided in advance rather than accidental.

clue.text: During break put up with complaint that's rather petty

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed in the midst of the break word

parts.note: to smash is to break

indicators.note: in a down clue put up means reading upwards, backwards

parts.note: an ill is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: In the interval, someone tolerates a grumble that's somewhat small-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up with' looks like tolerate, but 'put up' reverses ILL and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty in the sense of little, so rather petty is fairly little.

clue.text: Odd gem, one bizarrely being worshipped?

indicators.note: bizarrely means the letters are rearranged strangely

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A strange gem, one oddly venerated.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-divine figure, a being who might receive worship.

clue.text: Will once again need reforms in bank

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the bank word

parts.note: a bank of seats is a row

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A will needs reforms in the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is a verb: to bequeath again.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow again is to bequeath or bestow funds a second time.

clue.text: Busts saw, cutting article: that was careless!

indicators.note: cutting means removing a letter from the word

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
oops is the cry after a clumsy slip

explanation.surface: A saw cuts an object, and someone blurts out an apology for carelessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Police raids are busts, sudden swift descents on suspects.

clue.text: Bypass — a fast one?

definitions.meaning: to avoid or get round something
a trick, as in pulling a fast one

explanation.definitionFit: To evade something, and a sly trick or scheme.

clue.text: Trick on reflection mostly duff?

indicators.note: reflection reverses an image, so the word reads backwards
mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to dupe is to trick

explanation.surface: A trick, looking back, was largely a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' looks like useless, but plum duff is a British steamed pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff is a boiled pudding, and pud is the British short form of pudding.
